source.revision: main plus the release pull request for build maverick-public-dev-20261123.1 (release notes, rights review, changelog, readme, manifest)
source.dirty_delta: The build ran from builder/public-image/rootfs-overlay/ and build-root.sh with content identical to the files in main after the dev.7 pull request (the changed overlay files are etc/udev/rules.d/90-froodzos-internal-ro.rules and usr/local/sbin/fz-dtb-fixup.py; the boot image was built with build-sound-uki.sh and fz-dtb-fixup.py --enable-nvme).
source.note: The root is derived from the pinned Phase 1 root (sha256 22dde19c5a9e0b2a6e00f30cce7d0866d08159e1127871793553cd0478d1aacf) by builder/public-image/build-root.sh, built in six steps (r10 = the dev.3 root; r11 adds PKGS="pipewire-audio pipewire-pulse plasma-pa libgpiod" and the sound overlay; r12 adds pipewire-alsa and the shutdown drop-ins; r13 adds the fz-bootmnt-ro service; r14 to r16 add fz-sound-setup and its unit and launcher, the read-only internal-drive udev rule and the dev.5 version strings; r17 starts the sound set-up from a timer, fixes its --dry-run, adds fz-swap-lr and the dev.6 version strings; r18 replaces the udev read-only rule with one that runs blockdev --setro, updates fz-dtb-fixup.py and sets the dev.7 version strings), each a full system upgrade with PRUNE=1, the overlay files, a prebuilt ld.so.cache and size reduction.

inputs.uki_change: The first two boot entries use froodzos-maverick-dspN2.efi: the dev.4 sound boot image with a device-tree change made by fz-dtb-fixup.py --enable-nvme (internal NVMe PCIe controller and PHY enabled; the wake-gpios property of the controller node deleted because its root-port child repeats it). The third entry keeps the touchpad boot image, which does not enable the internal disk.
inputs.menu: output/grub.cfg.public14 (sha256 07e8aedd5486def27b5614260a2733d0f24b330d6bd3a42a29195cda388d2af1) generated from the dev.6 menu (grub.cfg.public13) by changing the version text and the boot image of the first two entries; three boot entries and a firmware entry, no submenu, no chain-loading; kernel options include kestrel_graphics_unbounded=1, sysctl.kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0, cow_spacesize=2G; no fz_autorun, fz_persist, fz_dsp or fz_tplg (the second entry adds fz_sound=1)
inputs.root_package_origin: 782 pacman packages (all unmodified Arch Linux ARM except the one project-built kernel); plus two unmodified upstream release tarballs (Helium, Zen) listed in pkglist.tsv
other_removals: usr/lib/firmware/updates (vendor firmware extracted from a Windows installation)
pacman keyring private key and revocation certificate
project-local overlay repository and its signature
four Arch Linux logo files (usr/share/pixmaps/archlinux-logo*) and the LOGO reference
firmware for other Qualcomm chip families and older Wi-Fi generations
development headers, introspection and cmake files

toolchain.squashfs: mksquashfs from squashfs-tools 4.7.5, xz, 128 KiB blocks (build-root.sh)
toolchain.grub: Arch Linux ARM package grub 2:2.16-1 (grub-mkstandalone, arm64-efi)

board_profile.firmware: none of the vendor 83N3 firmware is included; Arch Linux ARM linux-firmware-qcom (X1E80100/X1P42100 and video decoder files only after pruning), -atheros (ath12k only after pruning), -realtek and licence texts are included
board_profile.redistribution_status: reviewed 2026-11-11, see RIGHTS-REVIEW.md; ALARM publishes no explicit redistribution statement (accepted risk); GPL written offer in SOURCE-OFFER.md

test_receipts.name: native boots of the dev.7 boot image on the Lenovo 83N3 (two owner boots)
test_receipts.result: on 2026-11-23 the owner booted the first-entry boot image of this release (froodzos-maverick-dspN2.efi, identical sha256) from a private test stick with the released image's second-entry kernel options (fz_sound=1; the stick menu used a 3 GB instead of 2 GB RAM overlay and a root directory named froodzos-r17 or froodzos-r18), once with the previous root (r17) and once with the root of this release (r18, byte-identical to the released root, sha256 above). Both boots: desktop session started, no kernel oops or warning, the internal NVMe disk appeared (nvme0n1 with four partitions), Wi-Fi associated and stayed up, fz-sound-setup reported its source as the Windows DriverStore on the internal disk (mounted read-only), staged six files, the audio DSP went to running and the sound card X1E80100-LENOVO-Ideapad-3 and the speaker sink appeared with no typing. In the r18 boot the owner reported sound and Wi-Fi good, and the log recorded read-only flag 1 on the disk and all four partitions and zero write operations to the disk. The released image itself was not written to a stick and booted
test_receipts.scope: owner test, two boots on one laptop; private menu (3 GB overlay); the released image was not itself booted on the laptop; the cause of the dev.5 crash with an enabled controller is not proven (a deleted repeated GPIO property is the suspected fix)

limitations: Sound needs the owner's own audio firmware: the image contains none. fz-sound-setup reads it from the owner's Windows partition on the internal disk (mounted read-only; not possible if Windows is BitLocker-encrypted) or from a FroodzOS-firmware folder on the stick, copies six files into memory and restarts the audio DSP (command, or the second boot entry, which starts it about 75 seconds after boot). Left and right can come out reversed on some boots (cause not found; fz-swap-lr swaps them).
Graphics are software-rendered (llvmpipe) on a firmware framebuffer; there is no GPU acceleration. USB-C display output and alternate modes are not claimed.
Touchpad: the kernel driver binds and the pad works in an owner test; gesture quality is unconfirmed. The second boot entry keeps the user-space polling driver.
Battery level, charge state and USB-C power data work in an owner test; power management beyond that is not claimed.
Wi-Fi does not recover after suspend and resume; suspend and resume are not claimed. A memory-bandwidth monitor driver (bwmon) fails to load its table.
RAR is extract-only (UnRAR licence). Wine, Waydroid and QEMU are not included.
Helium and Zen are unmodified third-party releases; their trademark and artwork terms were not reviewed separately and the Helium signing key is not otherwise certified.
Browser sandboxes need unprivileged user namespaces; the image sets kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0.
Boot loader and kernel images are unsigned; Secure Boot must be off. The downloads are signed (SHA256SUMS.asc).
Opt-in persistence (fz_persist=1) was tested on hardware only on the private stick; whoever holds the stick can read what is stored on the persistent partition.
No vendor firmware is included. Default live accounts are those of the development image (user live, password live).
Arch Linux ARM publishes no explicit redistribution statement; the maintainer acceptance of the three-year written source offer is recorded at release approval.

The internal disk is visible to the live system. It is made read-only by a udev rule when it appears (blockdev --setro on the disk and every partition) and hidden from the desktop mount offer, so there is a short moment before the flag is set; the dev.5 and dev.6 rule did not work (the sysfs read-only attribute cannot be written) and the drive was in those releases not visible anyway. The cause of the dev.5 kernel crash with an enabled PCIe controller is not proven.
The release image itself was only emulator-tested; the owner tests used the identical boot image and (in the second boot) the identical root on a private stick, with the second-entry kernel options.
